# Power station size for a fridge during an outage

A power station for a fridge has to pass three checks. Surge decides whether it runs at all, and watt-hours decide for how long.

| Check | What you need | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Surge (peak) watts** | At least **1,300 W**, and up to ~2,400 W for large or older fridges | The compressor spikes at startup and a weak inverter trips immediately. |
| **Continuous watts** | ~250 W or more (typical fridge runs 100-250 W) | Almost any 1,000 W-class unit clears this. |
| **Watt-hours** | ~1,000 Wh for most of a day, ~1,400-2,000 Wh for a full 24 hours | The compressor cycles on and off, so average draw is far below the label wattage. |

Also look for a **pure sine wave** inverter, which is standard on reputable LiFePO4 units.

## Rules of thumb by outage length
- **8-12 hours:** about 1,000 Wh. A 1,070 Wh unit is estimated to run a typical fridge ~17 hours ([HomeGridHQ](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/)).
- **24 hours:** about 1,400 Wh by one conservative estimate ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/power-station-for-a-refrigerator)), or 1,600-2,000 Wh ([BlackBox Supplies](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage)).
- **2 days:** about 2,800 Wh. 3 days needs ~4,200 Wh, and expandable units or solar help here ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/power-station-for-a-refrigerator)).

## Size it to your fridge
1. Find the kWh/year on the yellow EnergyGuide label, or look up your model in the DOE's Refrigerator and Freezer Energy Rating Search Tool ([iTechGuides](https://www.itechguides.com/how-to-size-a-portable-power-station-for-a-refrigerator-and-essential-devices/)).
2. Average watts = kWh/year × 1,000 ÷ 8,760. An 18 cu ft ENERGY STAR fridge at 362 kWh/year averages ~41 W.
3. Needed Wh = average watts × 24 × days ÷ 0.85 (inverter losses) × 1.2 (headroom).

Side-by-sides with ice makers can average about double that, and hot kitchens or frequent door openings raise it. Keep the door closed during the outage. If you also want lights, a router or a medical device, add their watts and Wh.

## Models that fit
Prices vary, so check current listings.
- **~1,000 Wh (part of a day):** Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 (1,070 Wh, ~17 hours, about $449-799) and BLUETTI AC180 (1,152 Wh, 1,800 W with 2,700 W peak, about $399-699). Both are listed on the [BlackBox Supplies guide](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage).
- **~2,000 Wh (a full day or more):**
  - [BLUETTI AC200L](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac200l) has 2,048 Wh, 2,400 W output and is expandable to 8,192 Wh. It is $899 at BLUETTI's store, and the Dealectric page lists code AFF5OFF for $44.95 off. That link is an affiliate link.
  - [Anker SOLIX S2000](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/portable-power-station-for-refrigerator) has 2,010 Wh, 1,500 W with 3,000 W peak, and was listed at $699.99 after coupon.
- **Multi-day:** the EcoFlow Delta Pro 3 (4,096 Wh, ~2.8 days) is one option on [HomeGridHQ's list](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/), though it costs about $2,800.

I only have direct purchase links for the AC200L and Anker's own page, so for the others, use the guide pages above to find current listings.

**My suggestion:** if you want a full day of protection with some margin, aim for about 1,500-2,000 Wh with at least 1,500 W surge. If you only need to cover a few hours or two, a ~1,000 Wh unit is enough and cheaper. If you tell me your fridge's kWh/year or model, I can narrow it down.
